name: Palisades & Eaton Fires Los Angeles - Before & After Analysis
description: Satellite imagery of the Palisades and Eaton Fires in the Los Angeles area, California, captured before and after the fire event in January 2025. Combines cloud-free Sentinel-2 optical multispectral imagery (10-20m resolution) with Sentinel-1 SAR radar data (10-25m resolution) to enable fire extent mapping and damage assessment. Optical data shows visible/near-infrared reflectance for burned area detection. Radar data penetrates clouds and detects structural changes.
geocr:spatialBias: ["Dataset restricted to Los Angeles County (bounding box: -118.67°W to -118.16°W, 33.66°N to 34.34°N). Completeness depends on Sentinel's 5-6 day revisit cycle. Mid-latitude coverage is optimal; polar regions have gaps but do not apply here."]
geocr:samplingStrategy: ["All available cloud-free (≤10%) Sentinel-2 within ±15 day windows around fire event over Los Angeles County bounding box", "All available Sentinel-1 GRD acquisitions in same windows; varied orbit states (ascending/descending)", "Pre-event window: 2024-12-20 to 2025-01-05; Post-event window: 2025-01-15 to 2025-02-05"]
rai:dataCollection: ["Sentinel-2 data from ESA Multispectral Instrument (MSI) via Copernicus program; Level-2A surface reflectance atmospherically corrected by ESA", "Sentinel-1 data from ESA Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) via Copernicus program; Level-1C Ground Range Detected products via AWS Open Data", "Data selected around fire event dates (January 7-9, 2025) with cloud cover ≤10% for optical data"]
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset contains georeferenced satellite imagery of private residential properties in Los Angeles. While satellite imagery is publicly available, derivative products identifying burned homes require privacy-aware handling.
rai:dataLimitations: Sentinel-2 optical data limited by cloud cover; pre/post scenes selected for minimal cloud ≤10%
Sentinel-1 SAR not affected by clouds but has lower spatial resolution than optical data
Dataset represents only available cloud-free acquisitions; temporal gaps exist due to revisit cycles (5-6 days)
Fire perimeter boundaries not included; users must apply fire detection algorithms (Normalized Burn Ratio, coherence change detection)
Data includes ESA Level-2A atmospheric corrections only; users may need additional radiometric calibration
Ground truth validation data not provided; fire extent depends on user interpretation of spectral signatures
rai:dataBiases: Optical data affected by atmospheric effects (aerosol, water vapor) that alter spectral reflectance in smoke-affected areas
SAR backscatter affected by surface roughness changes from fire damage; requires multi-temporal coherence analysis
Sentinel constellation has polar orbit characteristics but does not affect mid-latitude coverage at Los Angeles
rai:dataUseCases: Fire extent and burn severity mapping
Land use and land cover change analysis
rai:dataSocialImpact: ["Enables rapid damage assessment supporting emergency response and resource allocation", "Fire extent maps inform evacuation planning and public safety communication", "Post-fire analysis supports insurance claims and disaster relief targeting", "Supports independent verification of fire impacts and transparency", "Caution: fire extent analysis may identify burned private properties; users should consider privacy implications when sharing derived damage maps"]
